rows.title: Hook 05
findings: The assigned ending collapses two different reactions: after lowering the vertical finger there is a second late eye closure and chin lift, then a final alert/pursed-lip close view.
The index fingertip rises beside the nose above the lip; it is not a drinking gesture. Finger remains extended under the chin for part of the late phase, then lowers in the final frames.
Camera briefly retreats/tilts upward around the late chin lift and returns close at the end; gentle bob alone underspecifies this.

sourceIntervals.action: Look screen-right with raised brows and mouth open, can held upright below the lips in the screen-right hand.
Turn toward the lens with widening eyes as the camera comes closer and the can lowers slightly. Keep the mouth open.
Glance screen-right and extend the index finger of the can-holding hand vertically beside the nose, above the open lips. Other fingers continue holding the can; do not take a sip.
Squint and briefly close the eyes while the index finger remains raised beside the face.
Reopen the eyes, lower the vertical finger to a more horizontal point beneath the chin and look toward the lens with knitted brows and pursed lips. Retain the can grip.

Close or narrow the eyes again and lift the chin, briefly parting the lips while the finger remains extended under the chin. The handheld viewpoint retreats slightly and tips upward, showing more ceiling.
Reopen the eyes and bring the questioning face close to the lens again, brows knitted and lips small/pursed. Lower the finger and can further, ending without a sip.

rows.title: Hook 06
findings: No new substantive action omission found: assigned prompt already has the sustained sip, can tilt/contact, lowered can, pursed lips/eye closure and final open-mouth reaction.
Numeric onset/hold/release intervals would make the long sip and short ending recovery less ambiguous. This is a timing refinement, not a newly discovered absent gesture.
